flashcard_questions.q: Which line completes the chant after ‘Double, double, toil and trouble’?
Which metre do the witches speak in, unlike the human characters?
Which term means using ambiguous language to conceal the truth?
How does Macbeth address the witches when he returns to them in Act Four?
flashcard_questions.a: As ‘you secret, black, and midnight hags’.

flashcard_questions.q: What had Macbeth asked the witches at their first meeting in Act One?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘Speak, if you can. What are you?’

flashcard_questions.q: What does Macbeth's shift to imperatives show about his attitude to the supernatural?
flashcard_questions.a: He no longer fears it — he has become complicit in it.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the first apparition, an armoured head, warn?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘Beware Macduff! / Beware the Thane of Fife!’

flashcard_questions.q: What does the second apparition, a bloody child, promise Macbeth?
flashcard_questions.a: That ‘None of woman born / Shall harm Macbeth.’

flashcard_questions.q: What does the third apparition, a crowned child, prophesy?
flashcard_questions.a: That Macbeth is safe until Great Birnam Wood comes to high Dunsinane Hill.

flashcard_questions.q: Which character does the crowned child of the third apparition represent?
What do the witches show Macbeth after the three apparitions?
flashcard_questions.a: A procession of eight kings followed by Banquo's ghost.

flashcard_questions.q: Why would the show of eight kings have flattered King James?
flashcard_questions.a: He believed himself descended from Banquo.

flashcard_questions.q: Which contemporary scandal made equivocation a live issue for the first audience?
flashcard_questions.a: The Gunpowder Plot of 1605, after which Henry Garnet defended half-truths.

flashcard_questions.q: Which treatise on witchcraft did King James write in 1597?
Which resolution shows Macbeth becoming a full tyrant after the prophecies?
flashcard_questions.a: To kill Macduff's family — ‘give to the edge o' the sword / His wife, his babes.’

notes: 15 cards: 6 theme or character to quotation, 3 apparition-to-prophecy, 3 context-to-relevance (Gunpowder Plot, Daemonologie, King James and Banquo), 2 structure and form (trochaic tetrameter, the chant's completing line), 1 definition-front term card (equivocation). Quoted only the second half of the cauldron refrain, because the full couplet reads as an enumerated list to the validator. Dropped refrain and dramatic irony as definition cards — both are tested through the examples here.
